note: THE SHELF's themes (iteration 005 S; ONE PRIMARY THEME, iteration 006 C3). A theme is ordered by the catalogue's `priority` and continues as 'TITLE · 2' past 5 GB of .lwm + .webp, with the next numeral; `numeral` is the theme's numeral when nothing before it splits. Titles and blurbs are data: rename them here.
rule: EVERY FINISHED MOLECULE GOES TO EXACTLY ONE THEME: the steps of `precedence` are read in order and the FIRST step the molecule meets names its theme (`app`: a molecule of the app's own table; `any`: it carries one of these tags — unless it also carries one of the step's `none`); a molecule that meets none goes to `rest`. In words (Josh, 2026-10-18): the app's own table is THE CLASSICS; nutrients and foods are LIFE AND FOOD even when they are approved medicines — vitamin, nucleobase, food, flavour and sweetener always, and amino acid, sugar and fat unless the row also names a drug class (painkiller … immune: ChEBI calls many drugs an 'amino acid' or a 'fat' by structure alone — mefenamic acid, enoxacin, valproate — and those stay medicines); every other approved drug or medicine word is MEDICINE; the textbook molecules (`classic`) are THE CLASSICS; materials, atmosphere, fuel, refrigerant, battery, explosive, plastic, solvent, gas and metal are MATERIALS, ATMOSPHERE AND FUEL; then the rest of life's words (life, steroid, neurotransmitter, scent, natural, alkaloid) are LIFE AND FOOD; then pollutant, toxin, pesticide and colour are MATERIALS; everything else is THE REST. Reorder the steps here to change it; tools/volumes/pack.mjs reads nothing else (`pack.mjs --candidates … --themes … --count-themes` prints the counts).

themes.title: The Classics

themes.title: Medicine
themes.blurb: Medicines and the molecules the body answers to: painkillers, antibiotics, heart and mind, hormones, and the medicines of the eye, lung, skin and gut.

themes.title: Life and Food
themes.blurb: The chemistry of living things and of the kitchen: vitamins, amino acids, sugars and fats, flavours and scents.

themes.title: Materials, Atmosphere and Fuel
themes.blurb: What things are made of and what the air carries: metals, plastics, solvents, fuels, refrigerants, explosives, gases and dyes.
